module_title: Salient Features - 42nd Amendment, Federalism, and Core Provisions
introduction: At this level, we look at how the Constitution balances different concepts—like rigidity with flexibility, and federalism with unitary control. We also focus on major changes made to the Constitution, especially the 42nd Amendment, which drastically altered several features.

core_concepts.title: Federal System with Unitary Bias
core_concepts.description: India has federal features (two governments, division of powers, written constitution, independent judiciary) but a strong unitary bias (strong Centre, single citizenship, all-India services, emergency provisions).

core_concepts.title: 42nd Amendment Act (1976)
core_concepts.description: Known as the 'Mini-Constitution' because it made comprehensive changes. It amended the Preamble for the first and only time, adding three words: 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'.

core_concepts.title: Blend of Rigidity and Flexibility
core_concepts.description: Article 368 provides for two types of amendments (special majority, and special majority with state ratification), making it rigid. Yet, many provisions can be amended by a simple majority, making it flexible.

core_concepts.title: Single Citizenship
core_concepts.description: Unlike the USA (which has dual citizenship—national and state), the Indian Constitution provides for only one citizenship. All citizens enjoy the same political and civil rights nationwide.

core_concepts.title: Universal Adult Franchise
core_concepts.description: Every citizen above 18 years has the right to vote without any discrimination. The voting age was reduced from 21 years to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988.

important_entities.name: K.C. Wheare
important_entities.significance: He described the Indian Constitution as 'Quasi-Federal' (Federal in form but unitary in spirit).

important_entities.name: Ivor Jennings
important_entities.significance: He called the Indian Constitution a 'Lawyer’s Paradise' because of its legalistic and complicated language.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Although India is federal in nature, the word 'Federation' is NOWHERE used in the Constitution. Article 1 describes India as a 'Union of States'.
Students often confuse the words added by the 42nd Amendment. Remember, 'Democratic' and 'Republic' were already there. Only Socialist, Secular, and Integrity were added.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: These are the only three words ever added to the Preamble, done in 1976.

exam_strategy_tips: The 61st Amendment Act (reducing voting age) is one of the most frequently asked questions in State PCS and SSC exams.
Always associate K.C. Wheare with the term 'Quasi-Federal'.
